hero.title: Projects and Outputs
hero.description: Delivery Worker Atlas operates as a shared infrastructure for research on platform work. We bring together and produce data, methods, and tools in collaboration with workers, researchers, and partner organizations, contributing to public debate on mobility, working conditions, data justice, and the future of work in cities.

projects.title: Territorialization of platforms and de-/re-territorialization of workers in Brazil
projects.description: This research investigates how app-based delivery work is distributed across urban space through the analysis of geolocation, earnings, and working-condition data, seeking to understand circulation patterns, areas of greater activity, and territorial inequalities.
projects.imageAlt: Map of delivery activity intensity in Rio de Janeiro

institutions: Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)
contribution: This research contributes to Delivery Worker Atlas by producing and analyzing geolocation, earnings, and working-condition data from delivery workers, expanding understanding of circulation patterns and the territorial inequalities of platform work in Brazil.

The results feed the DWA database, support the development of visualizations and territorial analysis methodologies, and strengthen the use of worker-generated data as a tool for research, advocacy, and data justice.

projects.title: The economics of platform work: earnings, costs, and sustainability
projects.description: This project analyzes the economic dynamics of delivery work across different platforms using data collected by Delivery Worker Atlas. The research seeks to understand remuneration patterns, the main operating costs, and the factors that affect the long-term sustainability of this activity.
projects.imageAlt: Delivery worker using a navigation app on a motorcycle

projects.title: Data, rights, and organization: technology for workers
projects.description: This research explores how data produced by workers themselves can contribute to rights advocacy, collective organization, and the construction of fairer technological alternatives. Drawing on Meu Corre and other Delivery Worker Atlas tools, the project investigates data justice practices, data governance, and forms of collaboration among workers, researchers, and civil society.
